title: Agent Edit Slide
objective: Determine a practical local cross-platform architecture that accepts slide templates or sample slides plus natural-language or Docs/Word/Excel requirements, edits and updates data while preserving visual fidelity, and returns a completed slide using agent CLI runtimes without API keys.

nodes.title: Agent Edit Slide
nodes.hypothesis: Determine a practical local cross-platform architecture that accepts slide templates or sample slides plus natural-language or Docs/Word/Excel requirements, edits and updates data while preserving visual fidelity, and returns a completed slide using agent CLI runtimes without API keys.
insights: Use a structured slide representation linked to native PPTX objects, rendered regions and source provenance; screenshots are verification evidence, not the editable source.
Use provider-neutral local CLI adapters and reuse user login state; do not collect or store API keys.
Prefer clone-and-fill plus constrained patch operations, with native object generation only where needed.
Make render-diff, semantic completeness, provenance and manual approval first-class quality gates.

nodes.title: Input and artifact understanding
nodes.hypothesis: Existing slide decks and office documents can be normalized into a structured intermediate representation for reliable editing.
insights: Use a structured slide representation linked to native PPTX objects, rendered regions and source provenance; screenshots are verification evidence, not the editable source.

nodes.title: Agent CLI orchestration
nodes.hypothesis: A local desktop/web app can safely orchestrate Codex, Gemini, Claude and similar CLIs without embedding provider API keys.
insights: Use provider-neutral local CLI adapters and reuse user login state; do not collect or store API keys.

nodes.title: Slide editing engines
nodes.hypothesis: Programmatic PPTX editing plus rendering/vision verification is more reliable than asking an LLM to directly author binary slides.
insights: Prefer clone-and-fill plus constrained patch operations, with native object generation only where needed.

nodes.title: Cross-platform local UX
nodes.hypothesis: A local service with a browser UI and platform-specific CLI adapters can support Linux, macOS and Windows.

nodes.title: Quality and safety
nodes.hypothesis: Render-diff, semantic data checks, sandboxing and human approval gates are required for production-quality output.
insights: Make render-diff, semantic completeness, provenance and manual approval first-class quality gates.

nodes.title: Screenshot-only representation
nodes.hypothesis: A screenshot plus OCR is sufficient as the primary editing representation for preserving editable PowerPoint structure.
nodes.reason: Screenshot/OCR loses native text boxes, charts, tables, grouping, z-order and editability; use it only as a visual verification signal, not the source of truth.

nodes.title: Direct LLM binary authoring
nodes.hypothesis: An LLM can directly manipulate PPTX binaries without a constrained intermediate model and still preserve complex templates.
nodes.reason: Open-ended binary mutation has high corruption and layout-drift risk; constrain actions through a slide IR and deterministic patch engine.

nodes.title: Paper-derived architecture
nodes.hypothesis: Combining structured content planning, edit-based reference slides, object-level execution and rendered verification is the strongest approach for template-preserving slide updates.

nodes.title: Evaluation and failure boundaries
nodes.hypothesis: A reliable slide agent must measure instruction fidelity, data correctness, structural preservation, visual quality and refusal quality separately.

nodes.title: Data-driven template updates
nodes.hypothesis: User-provided business templates plus external spreadsheet/document facts require provenance-aware grounding and chart/table consistency checks.
